messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER: GPU pool 'west-eu-gpu' reported saturation and queue growth > 95% at 2026-11-12T09:12:01Z. Severity: P2. Paging SRE oncall.

oncall-bot: auto-created incident #INC-20261112-084. Notifying #incidents, #eng-runtime, #eng-sre.

liz (SRE): I’m on it. seeing steady enqueue rate ~1.8k req/min, active waiting queue ~4.9k. Autoscaler not adding nodes for last 8m.

ken (Runtime): grabbing runtime metrics. I see a surge of CUDA Xid 31 in the driver logs on ~50% of nodes, kernels restarting, resulting in GPUs dropping out of pool. That reduces our effective capacity.

alex (Infra): Autoscaler events show 'scale attempt failed: quotaExceeded' and also 'maxPoolSizeReached' for west-eu. Customer reserved capacity used. Could be hitting project quota.

joe (Customer Ops): Maya, we have a handful of customers complaining about latency spikes in the last 10 min—some 5xx errors surfaced. CS is pinging the affected accounts.

maya (PM): Noted. Which SLAs are at risk? Any customer-facing mitigation we can do quick?

liz (SRE): SLA risk for Bronze+ paid customers in west-eu. Immediate mitigations in order: 1) reduce queued work (throttle retries), 2) triage nodes with Xid and cordon/drain, 3) fallback routing to other regions if possible.

ken (Runtime): Confirmed Xid logs:
```
[2026-11-12T09:05:12Z] GPU0: Xid 31: GPU HANG detected
[2026-11-12T09:05:12Z] driver: killing process pid=22456 (inference-worker)
[2026-11-12T09:05:12Z] nvidia-smi: GPU0 reset initiated
```
This matches OOM followed by driver resets. Memory pressure traces show kernel OOM killer on some nodes.

alex (Infra): Quick check: cloud quota for GPUs in west-eu: limit 120, current in-use 119. Autoscaler hit max. We can raise quota but that'll take support ticket (~1-2h). Short term option: spin new nodes in nearby region (west-eu-2) and route traffic, or shrink some low-priority pools.

autoscaler-bot: Autoscaler report: attempted scale +8 instances; 6 failed due to quotaExceeded, 2 queued. CurrentPoolSize=119, MaxPoolSize=120. Backoff active (exp backoff in 30s).

liz (SRE): Ken — can we mark nodes with Xid as 'unhealthy' and drain them automatically to stop autoscaler thinking they're healthy? If nodes are flapping them might be counted as capacity but unusable.

ken (Runtime): I’ll push a repair script to cordon+drain nodes showing Xid>3 in last 10m. Command I plan to run:
```sh
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l pool=west-eu-gpu -o name); do
  if kubectl logs $n | grep -q "Xid 31"; then
    kubectl cordon $n && kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data -l node=$n &
  fi
done
```
Will run after we notify oncall. Expect ~3-4 nodes to be drained.

alex (Infra): Draining will temporarily reduce schedulable GPUs but frees us from flapping ones. Meanwhile I can spin up 4 GPUs in west-eu-2 and update routing policy to allow cross-region routing for non-sensitive tenants.

maya (PM): Can we bias low-priority traffic (free tier, dev orgs) to the other region first to preserve paid customer capacity in west-eu?

liz (SRE): Yes — we have routing tags. Joe, please prepare a message to affected customers offering ETA and mitigation. Mention cross-region failover possibility.

joe (Customer Ops): Drafting now. Will include: "temporary mitigation: isolated compute in nearby region for non-prod; we are working on restoring full capacity in west-eu; expected partial restoration within 30-60 minutes."

ken (Runtime): Running cordon+drain now on flagged nodes. Observed node-12 and node-17 both show repeated Xid 31 and nvml resets. Draining...

autoscaler-bot: Noted: pool shrink observed after drains. CurrentPoolSize=115. Autoscaler backoff cleared; new scale attempts scheduled.

alex (Infra): Launched 4 VMs in west-eu-2 (g4x.8 equivalent). They are registering now. I’ll pre-warm model artifacts for the top 10 high-QPS models to reduce cold-start latency.

liz (SRE): Good. Ken — any chance these Xid errors are due to a recent runtime deploy?

ken (Runtime): We rolled runtime v1.42 to west-eu yesterday. Telemetry shows increased Tensor RT allocations for certain model families. Could be a regression in allocator leading to OOMs under bursty load. I’ll revert the runtime agent on a small canary set and see if error rate drops.

ken (Runtime): Reverting runtime on canary nodes (node-21..24).

liz (SRE): Observing metrics — Xid error rate on canary nodes drops to near-zero after revert. Non-canary nodes still show Xid. This points to runtime change.

alex (Infra): Given that, we should roll the revert more broadly while we investigate. But careful: rolling restarts will cause more drains. Propose: 1) scale out to west-eu-2 to absorb traffic, 2) gradually revert runtime, 3) monitor.

maya (PM): Prioritize paid tenant traffic to remain in west-eu if possible; shift dev/free to west-eu-2.

liz (SRE): Agreed. Implementing routing policy change now to favor west-eu for paid tiers.

autoscaler-bot: Routing update applied: paid->west-eu primary, fallback->west-eu-2. dev/free->west-eu-2 primary.

joe (Customer Ops): Notifying impacted customers now. (posted support tickets to affected accounts; included steps we’re taking plus ETA).

ken (Runtime): Expanding runtime revert in controlled batches across remaining west-eu nodes. Rolling batch 1/4.

liz (SRE): Monitoring queue length — down from 4.9k to 1.7k within 12 min. Request latencies for paid tiers improved from p95 2.3s -> 600ms for served requests in west-eu. Some backlog remains as we warm new nodes.

alex (Infra): Cloud quota request submitted for +20 GPUs for west-eu; support ticket #CLD-7891. ETA unknown. We still have some headroom in west-eu-2.

ken (Runtime): After the broader revert, Xid events drop significantly cluster-wide. Looks like runtime v1.42 had a bad allocator path under multi-tenant bursts. I’m opening an engineering follow-up (ENG-RUNTIME-20261112) to root cause and add regression tests.

maya (PM): Good. Any customer data loss or incorrect outputs?

ken (Runtime): No evidence of corrupted outputs. Timeouts and 5xx were the primary issues. We’ll run replay on a sampled set to verify output parity.

liz (SRE): Current status summary: - Effective capacity reduced earlier due to driver Xid/OOMs + autoscaler maxed at quota. - Immediate mitigations: cordon/drain flapping nodes, cross-region spillover, runtime revert. - Queue reduced from ~4.9k -> ~900 in 30m. - Paid-user p95 latency largely restored.

joe (Customer Ops): Customers notified and acknowledging. One enterprise customer asked for postmortem and ETA for permanent fix.

maya (PM): Please schedule postmortem and include action items: quota safety, autoscaler telemetry for node health vs reported capacity, runtime regression tests, and cross-region failover playbook.

ken (Runtime): Opening rollback/release notes and will add additional memory guardrails/alloc logging.

alex (Infra): Followups: request permanent quota increase or reserved capacity for west-eu, and a runbook change to allow emergency quota expansion automation if Xid-type failures are detected.

liz (SRE): I’ll own incident writeup draft. Can we meet a follow-up post-incident in 1h?

maya (PM): 1h post-incident sync works. Assigning owners: liz (incident writeup), ken (runtime RCA), alex (quota & infra mitigations), joe (customer comms).

oncall-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial restoration. Severity downgraded to P3 at 2026-11-12T09:45:21Z. Please continue followups in #incidents. :white_check_mark:

liz (SRE): Closing thread here. I’ll paste the incident summary to the channel and attach the postmortem link once available. Thanks team. :heart:
